gaps.sentence: Don't worry about the dog — it ___ at strangers, but it never bites.
gaps.hint: typical behavior takes the present simple
gaps.explanation: Characteristic, repeated behavior takes the present simple: barks.

gaps.sentence: I ___ you were coming today — nobody told me!
gaps.hint: state verb forbids the past continuous
gaps.explanation: 'Know' is a state verb, so its past form is the past simple: didn't know.

gaps.sentence: This perfume ___ of roses and vanilla.
gaps.hint: perceived smell is a state verb
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception like 'smell' are state verbs, so the present simple is used: smells.

gaps.sentence: This is the best pizza I ___ in years.
gaps.hint: superlative experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Superlative statements about experience up to now take the present perfect: have eaten.

gaps.sentence: Look at Sam — he ___ at that stranger again.
gaps.hint: look draws attention to this moment
gaps.explanation: 'Look' draws attention to something happening now, so the present continuous is used: is staring.

gaps.sentence: We ___ each other since primary school, so nothing surprises me about him.
gaps.hint: since primary school continuing to now
gaps.explanation: A state continuing since a past point takes the present perfect: have known.

gaps.sentence: She ___ two majors when she was at university.
gaps.hint: a completed period in the past
gaps.explanation: A completed past period takes the past simple: did.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the car tonight, so take a taxi into town.
gaps.hint: a future activity in progress as reason
gaps.explanation: The future continuous can express something in progress around a future time, here as a polite reason: will be using.
